part_title: Monitoring Model Quality, Service Health and Incident Response

scenes.title: Monitoring AI Systems
scenes.narration: Follow the five arrows at the top. User prompts and other real-world inputs reach an AI service such as Amazon Bedrock. Monitoring data is collected with CloudWatch metrics and configured invocation logs, S3 for appropriate evaluation records, and optionally a streaming pipeline for application events. Dashboards display trends, alarms detect thresholds, and notifications can alert the team. Engineers then investigate logs, query stored evidence with Athena where appropriate, and change prompts, data, safeguards or model configuration. The middle comparison matters: accuracy, precision, recall and F1 require labeled examples and an evaluation process; they are not automatically supplied as model-quality scores by Bedrock. Bedrock invocation monitoring can expose latency, token usage, throttling and service errors. CPU and GPU utilization belong to compute you operate, not the hidden hardware of a managed Bedrock model. On the bottom dashboard, latency rising or throttles spiking signals a reliability investigation; an accuracy drop is a different, evaluation-based problem. Treat the displayed chart values as illustrative, then verify the root cause before acting.
